title: Zone-Based Landscape Processing: Light Shaping, HDR, and Sky Techniques
summary: This instructional video presents a zone-based approach to landscape post-processing, emphasizing restraint and a stepwise workflow rather than a single 'crank-it-all-up' pass. The presenter explains breaking images into zones (sky, rocks, water, mountains, etc.), weighing global versus zone-specific adjustments, and building a coherent light path through staged techniques. Key practices include extracting shadow detail before expanding exposure, applying color and tonal shifts with non-HSL tools (temperature and tint), using the history brush for selective adjustments, selectively applying HDR-like texture to sky, and employing advanced methods such as manual focus blending, AI-powered removal suggestions, and sky replacement across shots. The workflow stresses avoiding over-processing, sequencing adjustments to guide the eye toward the light, and balancing multiple zones to maintain a natural, cohesive result while demonstrating both basic and more artistic enhancements for coastal landscapes.
topics: white adjustments (temperature and tint) over HSL
history brush and painting with selections
auto HDR in RAW and selective sky treatment
focus stacking and manual blend with clone stamp
simulated light source via whites and color grading
four-zone separation (sky, water, mountains, island) for complex scenes

sections.title: Philosophy and Zone Concept
sections.description: Introductory rationale for a restrained processing approach and the core idea that an image can be divided into zones (e.g., sky vs rocks) that may require different adjustments. The speaker notes that more zones mean more processing time and complexity.

sections.title: Light Direction and Transition Planning
sections.description: Discussion of shaping light by directing adjustments toward the source. The speaker identifies two lighting scenarios: light entering the frame from outside and light originating inside the frame, using side light to define form and guiding placement for subsequent edits.

sections.title: Shadow Extraction and Path to Light
sections.description: Technique to extract shadow detail first, then move adjustments in one directional flow (toward brighter, lighter tones). This framing helps avoid competing directional edits and creates a clearer path to the light.

sections.title: White Adjustments, Color, and History Painting
sections.description: Advocates using whites, temperature, and tint rather than HSL for color control. Demonstrates history painting workflows and selective painting with brushes and selections to apply adjustments to targeted zones.

sections.title: Auto HDR and Sky Selectivity
sections.description: Introduces an Auto HDR-like approach, including multi-pass adjustments to the sky and selective texture/contrast, while cautioning against applying HDR uniformly across the scene to avoid unnatural results.

sections.title: Four-Zone Separation and Atmospheric Work
sections.description: In more complex coastal scenes, the speaker outlines separating the image into multiple zones (sky, water, landscape, and an island) and using atmospheric adjustments to enhance depth, including dedicated masking approaches for hard-to-select edges.

sections.title: Sky Replacement and Composition Adjustments
sections.description: Demonstrates acquiring a different sky from another shot, cropping and aligning, and blending to preserve composition. Discusses considerations of light direction and space to support a convincing sky replacement.

sections.title: Simulated Light and Final Polish
sections.description: Covers creating a simulated sun and driving the composition with targeted dodging/burning and color grading to produce a cohesive, dramatic result while preserving overall color balance.

sections.title: Focus Blending and Manual Detailing
sections.description: Shows blending two focus positions with a hard-edge brush and clone-stamp workflow to produce a seamless focal balance across foreground and background elements.
